title: Courses Paid For Your Deploys
caption:
The deploy tool I pay for got 50% more expensive because people stopped buying programming courses.

Hatchbox went from $10 to $15 a server on Oct 1 — everyone, no grandfathering. The reason isn't servers. GoRails, the video-tutorial business that had been subsidizing Hatchbox development for years, will sign fewer new customers in 2026 than in its founder's first year in business. "AI has been brutal to most education businesses." Then, in the same 12 months, he shipped an MCP server for Claude Code.

I price my own stuff off what competitors charge. I never once asked what was quietly paying for theirs.

What's subsidizing yours?

slides.headline:
Courses Paid
For Your Deploys
slides.sub: Hatchbox, the Rails deploy tool, went from $10 to $15 per server on October 1 — new and existing customers, no grandfathering. The reason has nothing to do with servers.

slides.headline:
Fewer Than
Year One
slides.sub: GoRails, the video-tutorial business that subsidized Hatchbox development for years, will sign fewer new customers in 2026 than in its founder's first year in business. "AI has been brutal to most education businesses."

slides.headline:
Raise, Or
Get Jobs
slides.sub: His two stated options: raise prices and keep building full time, or put Hatchbox on the back burner and get jobs. He ruled out grandfathering because it would have left most revenue at the old rates.

slides.title: Then He Shipped MCP
slides.sub: Shipped in the same 12 months: a revamped API and an MCP server that wires Hatchbox deploys into Claude Code, Codex and Cursor.
